data.answer:
NotebookLM does not provide an official public API; the available MCP implementations function by extracting browser cookies from a managed session [1][2].

To authenticate, use the CLI command `nlm login` (or `notebooklm login` depending on your package), which automatically extracts and caches your Google session cookies, CSRF token, and session ID [1][3][4]. These are stored locally in an `auth.json` file [1][2].

For MCP server configuration, avoid hardcoding tokens in environment variables, as they rotate frequently [5][1]. Instead, rely on the CLI to manage the token lifecycle automatically [1][2]. If you must use environment variables for specific deployments, ensure `NOTEBOOKLM_BASE_URL` is set for Google Workspace instances [1][6].

data.answer:
To authenticate an MCP client with Salesforce, you must register an External Client App (ECA) in your Salesforce org [1][2]. Connected Apps are not supported [1][2].

In the External Client App Manager, enable OAuth settings, provide the specific callback URL required by your client (e.g., `http://localhost:8787/callback` for Cursor), and include the `mcp_api` and `refresh_token` scopes [1]. You must use the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE [3][4]. For web-based clients, you may additionally require a client secret [1]. Configure your MCP client using the consumer key generated by the ECA [2][5].

data.answer:
The Podio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server allows AI assistants to interact with Podio data [1][2]. You can connect using shared default credentials without an API key, or by generating your own Podio API key for better security [1][2].

To use your own credentials, generate a Client ID and Client Secret at your Podio account settings under the API Keys tab, setting the Redirect URL to https://mcp.podio.com [1][2]. In your AI platform's OAuth configuration, use these endpoints:

- Authorization URL: https://mcp.podio.com/oauth/authorize
- Token URL: https://mcp.podio.com/oauth/token [1][2]

data.answer:
Slack supports four authentication methods for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: Slack identity auth, Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), manual OAuth, and no authentication [1].

For manual OAuth, you must define an `external_auth_providers` block in your app manifest and reference it via `auth_provider_key` in your `mcp_servers` configuration [1]. The required redirect URI for your OAuth provider is `https://oauth2.slack.com/external/auth/callback` [1][2].

To exchange credentials for an access token, use the Slack user token endpoint: `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access` [3][4]. Enterprise-managed authorization (EMA) is also available as an alternative to standard OAuth [4].

data.answer:
Discord does not have a specific API feature called MCP credentials. Authentication for Discord applications is handled primarily through OAuth2 or Bot tokens [1][2].

To authenticate, you must register an application in the Discord Developer Portal to obtain a Client ID, Client Secret, and Bot Token [1][3]. You can then use these to authenticate via:

OAuth2: Use the authorization code grant or client credentials flow by interacting with the token endpoint at https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token [1].

Bot Tokens: Use your bot token in the Authorization header as `Authorization: Bot <TOKEN>` [2][4].

Provisional Accounts: For game integrations, you can use the Bot Token Endpoint at https://discord.com/api/v10/partner-sdk/token/bot to exchange external user IDs for access tokens [5].

data.answer:
DataForSEO uses Basic Authentication for its API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server [1][2]. You must use your unique API login and password, which are distinct from your dashboard account credentials and can be found in the API Access section of your DataForSEO account [3][4].

For standard API requests, include an Authorization header in the format: `Authorization: Basic <base64_encoded_credentials>`, where the encoded string is your `login:password` [1][4].

For MCP server configurations, you can provide credentials via environment variables (`DATAFORSEO_USERNAME` and `DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD`) or by passing the Base64-encoded Basic Auth header directly in your client's configuration [2][5][6].

data.answer: Firecrawl provides two primary ways to authenticate its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server: OAuth and API keys. For interactive clients, use the OAuth server URL `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`, which triggers a browser-based sign-in flow. For automated scripts, servers, or CI environments, use the base URL `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` and include your API key in the request headers as `Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>`. Never include credentials directly in the URL. If you are using a keyless connection, you are limited to the search, scrape, and parse tools.

data.answer: Neo4j MCP HTTP transport supports two per-request auth methods: Bearer token (for Neo4j Enterprise/Aura with SSO/OAuth/OIDC) and Basic auth (username/password). Configure your MCP client to send an Authorization header via mcp.json: Bearer uses “Authorization: Bearer <token>” and Basic uses “Authorization: Basic <base64(username:password)>” (base64 of “neo4j:password”). The MCP server reads credentials from the Authorization header by default; you can override the header name with NEO4J_HTTP_AUTH_HEADER_NAME. Sources: [1][2]

data.answer: Squarespace authentication for Commerce APIs uses either an API key or an OAuth 2.0 access token, both sent as an Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN header (with a User-Agent too) [1]. data.answer:
Notion MCP requires user-based OAuth 2.0 authentication and does not support bearer token authentication. To connect an MCP client to Notion, you must implement the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE.

The process involves discovering the server's OAuth metadata, generating PKCE parameters, performing dynamic client registration, and exchanging the authorization code for tokens. Once authenticated, you include the access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token when connecting to the Notion MCP server via Streamable HTTP or SSE.

data.answer: Zendesk MCP server connections exclusively support OAuth 2.0 authentication [1][2]. When configuring an MCP connection in the Zendesk Admin Center, you must provide the Client ID and Client Secret for your MCP server [1][2]. The Zendesk MCP client supports auto-discovery via standard well-known endpoints to identify authorization servers and scopes [1][2]. Stdio transport is not supported; only HTTP servers are compatible [1][2].

data.answer:
LiveAgent provides a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to connect AI tools directly to your account [1][2]. You can authenticate your MCP client using either a Bearer token or OAuth 2.1 [1].

To generate a Bearer token, navigate to your agent profile, select MCP in the left-hand menu, and click Generate token [1]. Copy this value immediately, as it cannot be retrieved later [1][3]. For OAuth 2.1, use the server URL https://YOURDOMAIN.ladesk.com/api/mcp; the client will automatically handle the discovery, redirection, and consent flow using PKCE [1][3].
